transcript: Welcome to the quick start tutorial on the 2D window tools. To start with, go to the Library tab and choose an avatar. I will choose the avatar Camilla. Double-click to bring the avatar into your scene. You can hide the Library tab, right-click and add background image. Choose your image. I am setting the scale to 50%. I am trying to make the image fit to where it would fit the avatar's size. 45% seems to be a good scale. Click on the Pattern Shapes button and click on the scissors to undock the tabs. Choose Polygon. Start to draw your pattern by clicking. By holding CTRL, you can build the curved areas. Hold SHIFT to make a straight line. I am setting the patterns to be transparent. I will also undock the Edit Pattern tools. Adjust the curves by using the Edit Curve Point tool. This time I am going to make straight lines and do the curves after. Use SHIFT again to make straight lines. Choose the Edit Curvature tool and make the curves. This is an alternate way to make curves. This is an alternate way to make curves. Using the Edit Pattern tool, click on a point, and you see the bezier handles and use them to adjust the curves. However, using the curve points is the preferred method for making curves. However, using the curve points is the preferred method for making curves. Again, use CTRL to create your curves. Again, use CTRL to create your curves. Use the Edit Pattern and click on the segment where I drew half of the sleeve. Unfold. Edit it to fit. Using the Edit Pattern tool, click on the pattern, right-click, and choose Symmetric Pattern with Sewing. The blue line around the pattern indicates this is a symmetrical pattern. Whatever I do to one side will happen to the other. Do the same for the sleeves. For the front pattern, use the Edit Pattern tool and select the line where the pattern should be mirrored. Choose Unfold Symmetric Editing with Sewing. This will create one pattern, and what you do on one side will happen to the other. This will create one pattern, and what you do on one side will happen to the other. Open the Internal Shapes tab, and draw half the pocket. Use CTRL to make the curve points. Using Edit Pattern, click on the line where the pattern should be mirrored and right-click and Unfold. Use Edit Pattern to create a pattern. Use loaf-heel bidet to create a line where the pattern should be mirrored. You can use the Edit Pattern tool to adjust as necessary. Use the Edge Curve point to adjust the curve if needed. Choose the Transform Pattern tool. Select the pocket internal line. Right-click and clone as a pattern. Here are the finished patterns.
summary: ```markdown # Quick Start: 2D Pattern Tools (3) Welcome to the quick start tutorial on the 2D window tools. ## Choosing an Avatar To start with, go to the **Library** tab and choose an avatar. I will choose the avatar **Camilla**. Double-click to bring the avatar into your scene. You can hide the Library tab by right-clicking and adding a background image. Choose your image. I am setting the scale to **50%**. I am trying to make the image fit to where it would match the avatar's size. **45%** seems to be a good scale. ## Drawing Patterns Click on the **Pattern Shapes** button and click on the scissors to undock the tabs. Choose **Polygon**. Start to draw your pattern by clicking. By holding **CTRL**, you can build the curved areas. Hold **SHIFT** to create a straight line. I am setting the patterns to be transparent. I will also undock the **Edit Pattern** tools. Adjust the curves by using the **Edit Curve Point** tool. This time, I am going to make straight lines and do the curves after. Use **SHIFT** again to make straight lines. ## Creating Curves Choose the **Edit Curvature** tool to make the curves. This is an alternate way to create curves. Using the **Edit Pattern** tool, click on a point, and you will see the Bezier handles. Use them to adjust the curves. However, using the curve points is the preferred method for making curves. Again, use **CTRL** to create your curves. ## Editing Patterns Symmetrically Use the **Edit Pattern** tool to click on the segment where I drew half of the sleeve. Unfold and edit it to fit. Using the **Edit Pattern** tool, click on the pattern, right-click, and choose **Symmetric Pattern with Sewing**. The blue line around the pattern indicates that this is a symmetrical pattern. Whatever I do to one side will happen to the other. Do the same for the sleeves. For the front pattern, use the **Edit Pattern** tool and select the line where the pattern should be mirrored. Choose **Unfold Symmetric Editing with Sewing**. This will create one pattern, and any changes made to one side will also occur on the other side. ## Drawing Internal Shapes Open the **Internal Shapes** tab and draw half the pocket. Use **CTRL** to make the curve points. Using the **Edit Pattern**, click on the line where the pattern should be mirrored, right-click, and choose **Unfold**. Use the **Edit Pattern** to create a pattern. Use **loaf-heel bidet** to create a line where the pattern should be mirrored. You can use the **Edit Pattern** tool to adjust as necessary. Use the **Edge Curve Point** to adjust the curve if needed. Choose the **Transform Pattern** tool. Select the pocket's internal line, right-click, and clone as a pattern. ## Final Patterns Here are the finished patterns. ```
